digest.overview:
Russia freed Michigan native Stephen Hubbard, 74, the last American Washington had declared wrongfully detained there, as U.S. envoys met Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on the Ukraine war. President Trump said Volodymyr Zelenskyy "has to want to settle this war." At a North Carolina rally, Trump again promised $5,000 payments if Republicans win, as polls show Democrat Roy Cooper leading the Senate race. CBS News found armed Homeland Security agents going door to door in at least six states asking about immigration status and voting. Vice President JD Vance declined to endorse Benjamin Netanyahu, a day after Trump backed him. More than 100,000 California state workers are striking for a day over a return-to-office order. A nor'easter threatens up to 4 feet of coastal flooding in North Carolina. Netflix posted $12.9 billion in quarterly revenue, up 12%.

Abroad, Russia hit Ukraine overnight with 186 drones and missiles, killing four people and striking a 24-story Kyiv apartment block. Iran said a third tanker struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio called a deal with Tehran "extremely difficult." France will deploy troops to back up police after the riots. North Korea said Kim Yo Jong inspected border units now in firing positions, and South Korea's top military officer called the threats "intolerable." Seoul is pulling more diplomats out of Ukraine, citing air-strike risks. China defended yttrium export curbs on Japan. A voter-roll purge has sparked nationwide protests in India. Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case. Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has lost both legs after being struck by a car.

home.overview:
LeBron James won his 76ers debut as Philadelphia spoiled the Knicks' banner night 106–100, with Tyrese Maxey scoring 28. Detroit beat Boston 121–113 despite 38 points from Paul George, and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 as Oklahoma City won 116–104 at San Antonio, where Victor Wembanyama missed his first 12 shots. Warriors at Lakers headlines 11 games tonight. In the NFL, the players' union called for a full investigation into Jalen Hurts' medical care, the 49ers lost Mike Evans to an Achilles injury, and Week 7 opens Thursday with the Patriots at the Bears. The World Series starts Friday with the Rays at the Brewers.

PSG beat Barcelona 4–2 in a Champions League thriller but lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a torn ACL, and Liverpool outlasted Villarreal 4–3 to join them on nine points. Phil Foden hit a hat-trick in Man City's 5–1 rout of AEK Athens, and Napoli edged Bodø/Glimt 4–3. Bayern host Arsenal tonight without Joshua Kimmich, while the Europa and Conference leagues follow Thursday. In the Championship, Wolves and Portsmouth drew 1–1, and El Clásico arrives Sunday at Barcelona. In the KBO, Kia finished a first-round sweep of LG with a 13–1 rout behind Kim Do-yeong's grand slam and now meets Samsung from Sunday.

brief: Kia swept LG 3–0 in the first round, routing the Twins 13–1 in Game 3 at Jamsil.
Kim Do-yeong hit a record-tying grand slam and was voted series MVP after three homers and eight RBIs in the series.
Na Sung-bum added two solo homers, and starter Keisho Shirakawa allowed one run.
The loss was the last game at the old Jamsil stadium.
Kia opens the best-of-five second round at No. 2 Samsung on Sunday at 2 p.m. KST in Daegu, with the Lions' Koo Ja-wook back from injury.
